transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, my body just feels a little out of my control lately? I mean, I'm sure it's nothing major, but my sister wanted me to come in. 

A few weeks ago, I was just really energetic—like, pacing around my apartment all night, writing down all these ideas for a supper club I want to start. It was actually a really productive time! But, um, lately, I've just been a bit... slower? My sister says it takes me forever just to put my shoes on before my shifts at the restaurant. I feel terrible making her worry, so I just wanted to make sure everything is okay. Is that... does that make sense to start with?
Can you tell me more about that energetic period a few weeks ago? Did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or irritable during that time?

Um... well, I guess... I hope it's okay to admit this, but I actually lost my job right before that. I got fired. Which is really embarrassing, I know, but... at the time, I didn't feel upset at all. I actually felt weirdly unstoppable? Just really, really excited about everything I was going to do next. 

But, um, as for being irritable... I feel terrible even saying it, because I really hate being rude to people, but... if anyone tried to question my plans or told me to slow down, I kind of... well, I'd blow up at them. It just felt like they were trying to ruin my life and hold me back. I'm usually not like that at all, I promise. I try really hard to be nice to everyone. Is that... does that help answer what you were asking?
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was consistently elevated or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, during that energetic period?

Oh, um... I'm actually not really sure? I want to give you the right answer, I promise, but... it's honestly a little bit of a blur? 

I mean, I was just so focused on my supper club ideas, I didn't really notice if the excitement was happening *all* day, every single day. I'm so sorry, I feel like I should know that for you! I just... I didn't keep track of the time very well, so I can't say for sure if it was constant like that. I hope that's an okay answer? I can try to think harder if you need me to.
Can you try to recall if there was a specific stretch of time during that energetic period when you felt consistently excited or irritable from morning until night, almost every day?

I... I really want to be helpful, Doctor, I do. I'm trying to think back... but it's just so hard to pin down. 

I mean, I don't want to say yes and give you the wrong impression, you know? It's just... I really don't remember feeling that way from the moment I woke up until I went to sleep, every single day. I was just really busy and, um, enthusiastic about my projects. I don't think it was this constant, overwhelming thing all day long. 

I'm so sorry, I know you're trying to figure this out and I feel like I'm not giving you very good answers. I just really don't think it was like that... is it okay that I don't remember it happening that way?
Can you think of any specific days or a stretch of days when you felt excited or irritable from the time you woke up until you went to bed, without much of a break?

I... I really wish I could give you a better answer. I don't want to make your job harder, I promise. But... no, I honestly can't think of any specific days where it was just... non-stop like that. 

I mean, I'm sure I had moments where I was just really focused and happy about what I was doing, but... not from the second I woke up until I went to sleep. That sounds so intense, and I really don't think I was acting that crazy or anything. I just had a lot of energy for my ideas. 

I'm really sorry, I know you've asked me a few times now. I just... I don't want to lie to you or make it sound worse than it was. Is it bad that I don't have a specific stretch of days to tell you about? I'm trying my best to remember, I really am.

Can you recall if there was a time when you felt unusually upbeat, high, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it felt like your mood was different from your usual self and stayed that way for most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

Um, well... I mean, there was a time, I guess, after I got let go from my job. I didn't want to bring it up because it sounds bad that I got fired, but... yeah, right after that happened, I didn't feel sad or anything. I actually felt, um, weirdly unstoppable? Like, really excited about everything I was going to do next. 

And, I mean, I guess it lasted for a few days, maybe? But the thing is... I did get a little bit frustrated sometimes during that. If people didn't understand my plans or if they told me I needed to slow down, I kind of... well, I might have blown up at them a little bit. It just felt like they were trying to ruin my life, you know? 

I know that sounds terrible, and I'm really not an angry person, I promise! It's just... I was so passionate about what I was doing. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you're looking for, I really want to make sure I'm answering this right for you.

Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt unusually upbeat, high, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it felt like your mood was clearly different from your usual self and stayed that way most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

I... I know we just talked about this, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

Like I was saying, it was right after I lost my job. It was definitely a few days in a row, maybe four or more, where I just felt... I don't know, completely unstoppable. Really, really excited about all these new ideas I had. But... I did get pretty irritable, too. 

I feel so bad admitting this, because I really try to be easy to get along with, but if anyone questioned what I was doing or told me I needed to slow down, I would just... I'd blow up at them. It felt like they were trying to sabotage me or ruin my life. I know that sounds like an overreaction, and I'm really sorry if that makes me sound like a difficult person. I was just so caught up in it all. Is... is that the kind of stretch you were asking about? I really hope I'm explaining it okay.

Can you confirm if there was a specific period lasting at least four consecutive days when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—such as feeling unusually upbeat, high, or irritable—and stayed that way for most of the day, nearly every day during those four days?

Yes, um, yes, I can confirm that. I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record, and I'm really sorry to keep bringing it up, but it was definitely that time right after I was let go from the restaurant. 

It was at least four days, for sure. I just woke up every day feeling... well, like I said, weirdly unstoppable. Just so incredibly excited about everything. But then, yeah, if someone tried to tell me my plans were too much or that I needed to slow down, I would just... I'd get so irritable. I'd blow up at them because it honestly felt like they were trying to ruin my life. 

I really hate admitting that part, because I swear I'm usually very easygoing. I don't like conflict at all. But during those days, it was just... constant. From morning until night, every single day. I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

During that four-day period when you felt unusually upbeat or irritable, did you also experience a decreased need for sleep — like you were able to go with much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Um, about my sleep... I actually don't think I noticed anything different with that. I really hope it's okay to say no? 

I mean, I was definitely super energetic during the day with all my plans, but I'm pretty sure I still slept normally at night. I didn't feel like I could just skip sleeping or anything like that. I'm really sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for... I really want to be helpful and make sure I'm doing this right for you. Is it okay that I didn't have that happen?

During that four-day period, did your mood stay consistently high or irritable throughout each day, without significant changes up and down, meaning it felt like a steady state of being unusually upbeat or easily annoyed?

Um, yes... yes, it was pretty steady. I really hope I'm explaining this right, I don't want to confuse you. 

But yeah, it wasn't like I was up and down every few hours. Like I said, after I lost my job at the restaurant, I just felt this constant... like, this unstoppable excitement. All day long. And the irritability was always kind of right there underneath it, you know? If anyone tried to tell me to slow down or questioned what I was doing, I'd just snap. I'd blow up at them because it felt like they were trying to ruin my life. 

I feel so terrible even saying that, because I really try to be a good person and treat people well. I promise I'm usually not like that at all. But during those days, yeah, that feeling was just... it was always there. Is that what you mean by a steady state? I hope that answers your question okay...

During that time when you felt unusually upbeat or irritable, did you also notice other changes like being much more active or productive than usual, having thoughts race through your mind, or getting involved in activities that could have risky consequences?

Um, yes, I definitely noticed being a lot more active. I hope it's okay to say that I was actually really productive during that time? Like, it wasn't a bad thing, I was just getting so much done. 

I had this... this nonstop energy, you know? I couldn't even sit through a whole meal or watch a soccer game on TV without jumping up. I just felt like I had to be doing something useful. So I'd be making all these phone calls, or sketching out ideas for new menus, or completely reorganizing the kitchen. 

I guess I just felt really motivated to turn things around after losing my job. It felt good to be so focused, honestly. I wasn't doing anything dangerous or risky, I promise. Just... really busy with all my projects. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of examples you're looking for.

During that time when you felt unusually upbeat or irritable and more active than usual, did you also experience racing thoughts or find yourself talking more than usual, perhaps in a way that others noticed and commented on?

Um, oh gosh... I actually feel really terrible now. I know I told you a few minutes ago that my sleep was totally normal, and I really, really wasn't trying to lie to you, I promise! I just... I didn't want you to think I was, you know, losing my mind or anything. But now that you bring up how my thoughts were working... 

I don't know if I'd call it "racing," because that sounds bad, and they were honestly really good, creative thoughts. But my mind would just jump from one thing to the next so quickly. Like, I'd be thinking about new recipes for my own place, and then suddenly I'm designing the logos in my head, and then figuring out how to pitch to investors, and then looking into renting a commercial space. Every single idea just set off three more. 

So... yeah, because of that, I actually couldn't sleep. I'd just be lying there with all these plans going a mile a minute. And I guess I probably was talking a lot faster too, just trying to explain all these concepts to anyone who would listen. 

I am so, so sorry for messing up my answer about the sleep earlier. I just really want to give you the right information and be a good patient. Is it okay that I corrected myself? I hope I'm not making your job harder...
Can you confirm if your unusually upbeat or irritable mood, along with the increased energy and activity you described, lasted for at least seven full days without a significant break?

Um, no, it wasn't seven days. I really hope that's okay, I don't want to mess up the timeline for you. 

It was just those four days that I mentioned earlier. After that fourth day, the energy kind of... just stopped. I don't really know why, but things just went back to normal, or well, I actually got pretty down after that. But the really upbeat, energetic part was just for those four days. 

Is that alright? I hope I'm not making things confusing by saying it wasn't a full week. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right information.
